reader_guide.headline: Use this page like a question map.
reader_guide.plain_answer: The site is not asking the reader to believe a roadmap. It starts with public questions, then points to definitions, reports, and proof surfaces that already exist.
reader_guide.useful_for_reader: AI learners, recruiters, founders, operators, and builders who want simple language before source links and technical proof.
how_to_read: Start with the question you already have.
Open the Learn link when a term is unfamiliar.
Open the proof link when you want to inspect examples, numbers, limits, or public snapshots.

website_scan.current_strength: The site already has proof surfaces: articles, reports, Learn, Proof Tour, public catalogs, benchmark numbers, limitations, heartbeat rows, and market context.
website_scan.main_question: How can a technical website explain AI systems clearly enough that a reader can understand the concept before asking for a meeting?
website_scan.reader_value: A modern AI site should behave like a guided interface: start with a question, explain the idea, show a proof surface, and state the limit.
interface_principles: Use definitions and examples instead of internal roadmap language.
Prefer inspectable proof links over private architecture details.
Use charts, rows, and public snapshots where numbers help the reader.
Keep private systems private while making the learning surface useful.

modern_questions.question: How do you make an AI answer with sources instead of just sounding confident?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: Teams want AI systems that can point back to the file, article, transaction, or report behind an answer.
modern_questions.plain_answer: Use retrieval augmented generation. The system searches a trusted source first, gives the model that context, then shows where the answer came from.
modern_questions.already_built_example: The Learn page explains RAG and the Proof Tour links public proof surfaces with evidence, limits, and reports.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you are checking whether an AI answer can be inspected instead of only trusted.

modern_questions.question: When is vector search better than keyword search?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: Search gets harder when a visitor asks in different words than the article or dataset used.
modern_questions.plain_answer: Keyword search looks for exact words. Vector search looks for meaning, so it can find a relevant passage even when the wording is different.
modern_questions.already_built_example: The Modern AI Stack Radar defines embeddings and connects them to RAG, observability, and proof pages.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you are comparing a normal search box with an AI search or knowledge assistant.

modern_questions.question: If you have two AI components, how do you connect them without creating a messy system?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: Modern AI work often has separate parts: retrieval, tools, memory, evaluation, user interface, and approval gates.
modern_questions.plain_answer: Give each component a clear contract. One part should know what it receives, what it returns, what it is allowed to do, and what gets logged.
modern_questions.already_built_example: Proof Tour shows connected lanes for AML, agent coordination, heartbeat rows, governance, reports, and learning concepts.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you are trying to understand how small AI pieces become one usable workflow.

modern_questions.question: How do you know an AI workflow improved instead of just changed?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: A model can feel better while becoming less reliable on edge cases.
modern_questions.plain_answer: Use eval rows. Pick sample questions, expected behavior, pass or fail criteria, and notes. Then compare changes against the same set.
modern_questions.already_built_example: Reports shows benchmark-style values, limitations, and method notes so numbers are not floating claims.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you are reviewing AI output quality or deciding whether a change is actually better.

modern_questions.question: What should an AI agent be allowed to do by itself?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: Finance, healthcare, and compliance workflows need role boundaries, approval gates, and reviewable actions.
modern_questions.plain_answer: Start with roles. Some actions can be read-only, some require review, and some should stay human-only. The log is part of the product.
modern_questions.already_built_example: Learn defines RBAC, audit logs, tool calling, and MCP as one governance pattern.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you are thinking about AI agents in regulated or high-trust workflows.

modern_questions.question: Can a technical portfolio explain itself before the first call?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: Recruiters, customers, and collaborators usually need a fast path from claim to proof.
modern_questions.plain_answer: A proof page should answer four things quickly: what exists, what evidence supports it, what the limits are, and where to click next.
modern_questions.already_built_example: Proof Tour gives a guided route through AML, agent coordination, heartbeat, governance, reports, and modern stack signals.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you want to inspect technical work without reading the whole archive first.

modern_questions.question: How do you show AI work without exposing private systems?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: Technical work needs proof, but proof should not leak keys, paths, client data, infrastructure, or employer details.
modern_questions.plain_answer: Show public-safe artifacts: summaries, screenshots, manifests, synthetic examples, public APIs, and limits. Keep private operations out of the public page.
modern_questions.already_built_example: AI Intelligence shows public heartbeat rows, market context, and snapshot limits without private infrastructure details.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you need to present technical work while protecting security and privacy.

modern_questions.question: What turns a local AI demo into something reliable enough to run again?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: A demo becomes stronger when it can be packaged, health-checked, monitored, and redeployed.
modern_questions.plain_answer: Reliability comes from repeatable setup, clear environment boundaries, health checks, logs, tests, and rollback notes.
modern_questions.already_built_example: Learn maps Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, observability, and system health into one reliability layer.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you are deciding whether a demo is only a clip or something that can be operated.

modern_questions.question: What makes an AI project feel like engineering evidence, not a blog claim?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: Technical reviewers want methods, numbers, source links, limitations, and repeatable artifacts.
modern_questions.plain_answer: Evidence needs context. A number should say what was measured, where it came from, what it does not prove, and how a reader can inspect it.
modern_questions.already_built_example: Reports collects metric cards, benchmark bars, capability coverage, notes, and public-safe source links.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you want to judge whether an AI project has substance behind the writing.

modern_questions.question: What makes a website feel like an AI system instead of a static brochure?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: Modern AI websites increasingly behave like interfaces: searchable, interactive, refreshed, source-linked, and useful without a sales call.
modern_questions.plain_answer: The page should help the reader do something: ask, inspect, compare, learn, refresh, or follow evidence.
modern_questions.already_built_example: AI Intelligence refreshes public market data in the browser and shows public-safe heartbeat rows with limits.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you want a website to teach, explain, and show motion without overexposing the system behind it.
